claims_made_by_source.claim: "Reality is that which, when you stop believing in it, doesn't go away." (PKD's 1972 one-sentence definition).
Spurious realities are manufactured by the media, governments, corporations, and political/religious groups, and delivered into people's heads by electronic hardware.
PKD says he likes to build universes that fall apart, and confesses 'a secret love of chaos'; the old must perish so the authentic human can live.
In writing Flow My Tears (1970), PKD unknowingly retold incidents and names from the Book of Acts (Felix, Jason, the apostle Philip meeting a black stranger on the road).
PKD reports precognition: after finishing the novel he met a real nineteen-year-old Kathy with a boyfriend Jack who was secretly tied to a police inspector, matching his fictional character.
A week after Flow My Tears was released (Feb 1974), the golden-fish sign worn by a delivery woman triggered anamnesis: PKD remembered being a secret Christian under Rome awaiting Christ's return.
PKD's theory: 'time is not real,' and a permanent landscape — the world of the Bible, circa A.D. 50, the period of Acts — underlies the visible world of change.
Ubik (in the novel of that name) is the Logos: 'I am the word and my name is never spoken... I am Ubik but that is not my name.'
The authentic human is one who instinctively knows what he should not do and refuses — saying 'no' to the tyrant and calmly taking the consequences.

important_passages.excerpt: Reality is that which, when you stop believing in it, doesn't go away.

important_passages.excerpt: I suddenly experienced what I later learned is called anamnesis — a Greek word meaning, literally, 'loss of forgetfulness.'
important_passages.why_important: First-person account anchoring the dictionary term 'anamnesis' and the 2-3-74 cluster.

important_passages.excerpt: The authentic human being is one of us who instinctively knows what he should not do, and... will balk at doing it.
important_passages.why_important: PKD's positive ethic; the essay's answer to its second question.

uncertainties: PKD explicitly frames the time-is-unreal / A.D. 50 theory as provisional: 'The answer I have come up with may not be correct, but it is the only answer I have' (line 155).

The 'most powerful man... judged and condemned' between Feb and Aug 1974 is never named; PKD says he would 'prefer not to say,' though the Yorba Linda / 'all the President's men' cues point unmistakably to Nixon (lines 251–253).
This is lane-B self-report: it records what PKD said he experienced and theorized, not corroborated events.
